name: Spotted-wing drosophila
summary: A vinegar fly that lays eggs in ripening berries — a monitoring-and-threshold pest, not proof a named farm has an outbreak.
what_is_it: Spotted-wing drosophila (Drosophila suzukii, SWD) is a vinegar fly that can oviposit in ripening, still-firm fruit. Soft berries (raspberry, blackberry, blueberry, strawberry) are all hosts. Identification and trap counts matter because not every small fly in a planting is SWD, and calendar spraying is not the same as IPM.
why_it_matters: News about 'SWD pressure,' export holds, or a region 'losing fruit to vinegar fly' is often this pest. It changes harvest timing, sanitation, and whether a protected-culture or open-field program can keep packable fruit. A press mention is not a field diagnosis.
how_evaluated: Adult traps, salt or drowning tests for larvae in fruit, and damage counts versus a regional threshold. Extension guides update labels and resistance; those dates matter. There is no single SWD score for a company.
what_affects_it: Crop, canopy humidity, harvest interval, nearby wild hosts, and whether fruit is left in the field. Protected culture changes the pest complex; it does not make SWD impossible.
how_to_interpret: Treat SWD in intelligence as a named-pest framework. Do not read this page as a spray schedule or as evidence that a competitor's fruit is infested. Pair with IPM. Specific products and thresholds belong in the current regional guide, not here.

berry_notes.note: Caneberries are highly attractive hosts; thin fruit skin and frequent picks are why SWD shows up in raspberry and blackberry harvest talk.
Blueberry SWD risk rises as fruit colors and as harvest intervals stretch; process vs fresh packs have different tolerance for larvae, not different biology.
Strawberry can be a host, especially where ripe fruit sits; plasticulture sanitation and pick interval are the usual commercial levers, not a variety 'immunity' claim.
Same caneberry host story as raspberry; trailing types with dense canopies can be harder to monitor and pick clean.
